items.question: From whom must this teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The mortal world contains lowest men
items.inference: This teaching should be carefully hidden from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

compound describing tested recipient; sandhi within token

items.question: To what kind of recipient may this teaching properly be given?
premises: The recipient should be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching should be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

rows.grounds: locative in colophon context; compound candradvīpa-vinirgata

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the section emerged from Candradvīpa?
items.inference: The fifth chapter concludes in the section emerged from Candradvīpa.
uncertainties: candradvīpa+vinirgate may refer to a textual section or place; taken as a section title.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the section that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of Kaula become known?
premises: The determination of Kaula is known
The lord of Kaulas is addressed
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of Kaulas, the determination of Kaula has become known.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what reality does the soul dissolve, and what complete explanation follows?
premises: The locus of dissolution is questioned
items.inference: The speaker asks to be told where the soul dissolves and to receive the full account.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme attributes define the ultimate reality identified as that soul?
premises: That reality is partless and eternal
That reality is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The soul in its highest sense is defined as supreme, partless, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul further identified in terms of haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The supreme one is identified as the soul
That same one is called haṃsa
That one is described as power and individual
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as the haṃsa, characterized as power and individual.
uncertainties: śakti+pudgalaḥ is ambiguous; taken as a compound characterization rather than two separate entities.
items.plain_english: He who is the supreme soul is indeed the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: In what form is the vital air present within all living beings?
premises: Air is present in all beings
The air is described as wind-filled
items.inference: The vital air, filled with breath, is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement of saṃsthitam with vāyuḥ is irregular; sense taken as describing the air's presence.
items.plain_english: The air, filled with breath, is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the physical body?
premises: The moment of leaving is decisive
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and inwardly received according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
The goddess is addressed as witness
items.inference: This teaching is heard in the ear as it has come down through traditional succession.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the immediate effect of merely hearing this knowledge?
items.inference: Even mere hearing of this knowledge has a significant effect.
uncertainties: The main clause continues in the next verse; this verse states the means.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, simply heard,

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to freedom from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The state aimed at is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ is syntactically difficult here; taken as referring to an ascetic discipline or state.
items.plain_english: whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state free from bondage.

items.question: What benefits follow for the practitioner freed from all diseases?
premises: The practitioner becomes free from all diseases
items.inference: Freed from all diseases, the practitioner gains union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul?
premises: The teaching concerns practice of the soul
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: To which resolved and fully endowed person may this teaching be given?
premises: The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to one who is fully endowed and firmly resolved.

items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a firmly resolved mind.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, born of the yoginīs, must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: sambhavam may qualify sāraṃ or stand in apposition; taken as describing its origin.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after the veil of ignorance is struck away?
premises: The body was struck by ignorance
items.inference: Now the body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is declared pure.
uncertainties: deham appears in accusative form but functions as subject in sense.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The method is an auspicious deception of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious means of deceiving time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can truly be destroyed by this teaching?
items.inference: The speaker assures without doubt that this teaching explains how death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I will tell you—there is no doubt—how death is destroyed.

items.question: Why can even a wise person be afflicted at the source of nectar and essence?
premises: The locus is the tip of nectar
The means involves essence of juice
Even a wise person can burn
items.inference: Even the wise may suffer burning at the subtle source of nectar and essence.
uncertainties: The imagery is compressed and may refer to a yogic physiological locus.
items.plain_english: Even a wise person may burn at the tip of nectar by the essence of its juice.

items.question: What yogic technique at the root of tongue and palate counters this affliction?
premises: A specific bodily locus is used
The air should be drawn in slowly
items.inference: One should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing the breath at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the air.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this breath technique continuously for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this technique destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom results from mastery of this yogic practice?
premises: The body may be bitten by great serpents
In this case poison does not enter
items.inference: Through this practice, poison does not enter the body even when bitten by great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
